book: 024 - Bullshit and Philosophy - Guaranteed to Get Perfect Results Every Time

chapters.relation: First part of the editors' introduction, recounting how Harry Frankfurt's slim On Bullshit, after two decades circulating only among academic moral philosophers, spent twenty-six weeks on the New York Times bestseller list and outsold any commercial philosophy book. Reisch and Hardcastle treat the book's popularity as a puzzle worth explaining: a technical exercise in conceptual analysis struck a public nerve. The chapter uses Frankfurt's own definition of bullshit as indifference to truth as the anchor for everything that follows.

The editors answer why On Bullshit hit a nerve using Jon Stewart's Daily Show interview with Frankfurt, where the audience laughed at the claim that the bullshitter does not care whether what he says is true. The unspoken elephant in the room was the Iraq war: the claims about weapons of mass destruction, remote-controlled delivery devices, and 9/11 complicity turned out, in the editors' words, to be best described by that word. They argue readers embraced the book as 'bullshit without tears,' a cushion of humor letting them approach the war's deceptions abstractly rather than face the disturbing political questions directly.

'The Year in Bullshit' catalogues the fraud climate surrounding the book's success: James Frey's fabricated memoir A Million Little Pieces exposed on Oprah, the wholly invented author J.T. Leroy, product placement and paid word-of-mouth advertising blurring the line between ads and ordinary conversation, and scientific fraud in pharmaceutical and federal research. It invokes Karl Popper's claim that science deserves respect precisely because it falsifies its own claims, presenting headlines about fabricated results as that ideal fading. Frank Rich's verdict that 'such distinctions have long since washed away in much of our public life' supplies the chapter's explanation of the book's appeal as cultural despair.

'The Dream of a Bullshit-Free Culture' argues Frankfurt revives a centuries-old philosophical tradition: Socrates searching for genuinely wise people rather than purveyors of hearsay, Descartes' Meditations discarding every belief short of certainty, and Hume's forkcondemning divinity-school metaphysics that contains neither abstract nor experimental reasoning to the flames. The twentieth-century apotheosis is the Vienna Circle, whose Rudolf Carnap dissected Heidegger's 'Das Nichts selbst nichtet' as mere appearance of meaning, calling metaphysicians 'musicians without musical ability'. The editors cast Frankfurt as the latest carrier of this Enlightenment anti-bullshit torch, with the book's popularity reconnecting seminar-room philosophy to the marketplace and voting booth.

chapters.file: ch09 - I - To Shoot the Bull.md
chapters.relation: The Part I introduction, 'How This Book Came to Be,' explains what the volume is and is not: not a bullshit-detector manual but discussions and criticisms of Frankfurt's essay, including what it means to propose a theory of bullshit or articulate the structure of a concept. It previews each contributor: Kimbrough on why we let bullshit slide, Preti's use of G.E. Moore as a bullshit-free exemplar, Reisch's two-conversations account, Taylor on cognitive foibles, Bernal on personality pathology, and the Part II definitional debate between Frankfurt and G.A. Cohen's 'unclarifiable unclarity'. It frames philosophy itself as one of our best defenses against bullshit.

chapters.file: ch10 - Chapter 1 - On Letting It Slide.md

chapters.relation: Scott Kimbrough opens his essay with his six-year-old daughter shouting through a window that the house painter's smoking is unhealthy, and William Ian Miller's Faking It dictum that truth is seldom a defense. He takes up the puzzle Frankfurt left as an 'exercise for the reader': why our attitude toward bullshit is more benign than toward lying, even though Frankfurt defines bullshit as indifference to how things really are and therefore the greater enemy of truth. The chapter promises to solve the puzzle Frankfurt posed but never attempted.

Applying Frankfurt's definition strictly, Kimbrough argues much of civility is bullshit: coerced childhood apologies are 'humiliation rituals' where truth is the last thing wanted, politeness is benign hypocrisy that saves people pain, and the Super Bowl ad or the silly communist-professors editorial is valued as entertainment. We also tolerate PR and advertising bullshit out of respect for the ends served, from Exxon's green image to spin by teachers and military recruiters. His answer to Frankfurt's puzzle: we sympathize with bullshitters doing their jobs and contemptuously dismiss their victims as suckers who deserve their fate.

Kimbrough turns to when bullshit becomes intolerable: the philosophy-slam regulars' dismissive 'That's bullshit,' the girlfriend's indictment in The Black Eyed Peas' 'Shut Up,' and the boss's team-builder rationalization for passing you over for a promotion. He leans on Orwell's 'Politics and the English Language' and Nineteen Eighty-Four to show political euphemism ('collateral damage,' 'smart bomb') as the language of power, tolerated because repeating spin is easy and going along with bullshit is going along with power. The chapter closes on the danger of politicians believing their own bullshit, setting up the self-deception question of how one person can play both bullshitter and dupe.

Kimbrough resolves the self-deception paradox using Alfred Mele's Self Deception Unmasked: like the cuckolded husband who masks evidence of infidelity, the self-deceiver biases evidence-gathering rather than playing deceiver and dupe at once. Since Mele shows unintentional motivated belief is common (94% of professors rate themselves above average), bullshit like the entrenched prejudice that 'smart boys are smarter than smart girls' can arise without intent, which is G.A. Cohen's opening against Frankfurt's process-centered definition. Against Cohen's output-centered alternative, the conservative-talk-radio fan who builds his own conclusions on cherry-picked propaganda shows a product can be perfectly clear yet still bullshit, produced through self-deception.

Kimbrough defends calling alchemy bullshit even though Isaac Newton pursued it blamelessly: the charge's function is to excuse us from taking hopeless methods seriously, not to insult the theorist. His killer analogy sorts cases: the intentional bullshitter is the murderer, the self-deceived talk-radio fan the negligent driver who kills while reading, and Newton the blameless driver beside whom the pedestrian darts, with the pejorative resting on the method or theory rather than the person. This methodology shift lets him keep Frankfurt's insight that how bullshit is produced matters while conceding Cohen's point that it can be unintentional, though he admits even philosophy's status may never be settled.

chapters.file: ch16 - Chapter 2 - A Defense of Common Sense.md
chapters.relation: Concluding his essay, Kimbrough observes people call bullshit whenever their values are threatened, so the bottom-line businessman dismisses ethics talk and investigations of his dodgy accounting as bureaucratic bullshit, and the linguist may dismiss armchair conceptual analysis itself. He rejects a subjective definition of bullshit as whatever provokes disdain, endorsing Frankfurt's anti-subjectivist closer that 'sincerity itself is bullshit,' and concludes bullshit must be recognized and restricted to justifiable uses rather than eradicated. He closes with Orwell's advice from 'Politics and the English Language': simplify your English so that a stupid remark's stupidity is obvious even to yourself.

Consuelo Preti lays out Frankfurt's indifference-to-truth account and G.A. Cohen's academic bullshit as disregard for meaning, then argues both leave out bullshit's third element: the audience it needs. Bullshit, she says, sells us on our own estimation of what matters, from the Dior handbag to the guy bullshitting his way into bed or tenure. Reviewing the James Frey affair and Oprah's initial claim that truth was irrelevant because the story inspired, she proposes G.E. Moore's uncompromising commitment to truth and meaning as the model for resisting bullshit in the street and the seminar room.

Preti dissects l'affaire Frey: if Frey intended to palm off invented events as memory, he lied and his publishers committed fraud, but if they did not care either way, it was bullshit, and what exposed the menace was Oprah's own avowal that it did not matter whether the story was true. She argues inspiration tied to an assumed true story is sabotaged by discovering it false, so Oprah's retraction ('I left the impression that the truth does not matter') shows bullshit nearly turned even her head. The strategy she draws is to turn bullshit's need to be believed against itself, and for an exemplar of resolute caring about truth she reaches to G.E. Moore.

Preti builds the Moore exemplar from biography: with Russell and Wittgenstein at Cambridge, Moore founded analytic philosophy, demolished Absolute Idealism in the 1899 'The Nature of Judgment,' and wrote Principia Ethica, which the Bloomsbury group treated as their religion. Russell's autobiography joke about the only lie Moore ever told and Woolf's 'tenacity of a bulldog' portrait of his passion for truth set up Keynes's description of Moore's method, 'What exactly do you mean?'. The key episode is Moore's public apology for losing patience with a question he took to be merely vexatious, showing that what Moore could not tolerate was precisely bullshit.

chapters.file: ch20 - Chapter 3 - The Pragmatics of Bullshit, Intelligently Designed.md
chapters.relation: Preti's conclusion deploys Moore's 'A Defence of Common Sense' against philosophers who answer 'Do you believe the earth has existed for many years past?' with 'It all depends on what you mean,' a view Moore called as profoundly mistaken as any can be. She extracts a practical anti-bullshit strategy: dogged Moorean insistence on clarity, since bullshit's scorn for truth must stay masked and needs us to be less inquisitive. Her 'paradox of bullshit' is that truth and meaning do not matter to bullshit but bullshit must make itself matter to us, so caring about the truth-false distinction puts it on a short leash.

chapters.file: ch21 - The Example of Intelligent Design.md
chapters.relation: George Reisch opens his essay with Frankfurt's unsolved puzzle: if bullshitters are more dangerous to truth than liars, they should be punished more, yet we are more tolerant of them, a puzzle Frankfurt admitted on radio he really does not understand. He diagnoses the puzzle as a symptom that Frankfurt's definition took a wrong turn. The remedy requires distinguishing the semantic from the pragmatic analysis of language, and the new definition it yields will both cover Frankfurt's own examples and explain our tolerance of bullshit.

chapters.file: ch22 - A Definition of Bullshit—New and Improved!.md
chapters.relation: Reisch offers the Intelligent Design movement as a paradigm of bullshit Frankfurt could not have used in the 1980s: like advertisers and politicians, ID urgently needs public approval ('teach the controversy') and is trying to get away with something. He traces ID's descent from constitutionally defeated creation science through Philip Johnson's Darwin on Trial, showing how Johnson speaks of evidence and naturalism to scientists while telling evangelical audiences that the real enemy is cultural modernism's tolerance of promiscuity and atheism. Judge Jones's Kitzmiller ruling that ID is 'a mere re-labeling of creationism' confirms what the bullshit was covering.

If ID is bullshit, Reisch argues, Frankfurt's definition fails, because Johnson and his followers are not indifferent to truth; they are devoted to other, rotten truths about modernism and even to elevating regard for truth in the culture. Frankfurt's error was writing of 'the truth' as a single unitary thing everyone but the bullshitter agrees on, when our beliefs about how things really are are diverse and contradictory. Bullshitters conceal a commitment to other truths and an agenda inspired by them, since revealing those truths would be embarrassing, unpersuasive, or, as with ID, unconstitutional.

Even Frankfurt's bull-session example (with its Animal House atom-of-a-fingernail bit) shows relaxed talk serving other truths: self-image, reputation, and whether the apple of one's eye is impressed. Detergent slogans and politicians' rolled-up sleeves likewise run two conversations at once, one overt (clean clothes, policy) and one concealed (self-image, likeability), each resting on truths the bullshitter takes quite seriously. Reisch's definition follows: bullshit is the orchestration of at least two engagements between bullshitter and bullshitee, one concealed within or downplayed alongside the other, so indifference to truth is absent or only partly in play.

chapters.file: ch25 - Solving Frankfurt’s Puzzle, or, Baseball, Hot Dogs, Apple Pie, and Bullshit.md
chapters.relation: Reisch explains Frankfurt's blind spot through the historical neglect of pragmatics: even Carnap took for granted that any complete theory of language must include how language is used in context, yet analytic philosophy came to favor semantics, as the Cambridge Dictionary's twenty-six semantics entries against seven pragmatic ones attest. Since bullshit's essence lies in using speech to hidden purposes, it is an essentially pragmatic, not semantic, phenomenon, which also shows the Frankfurt-Cohen debate (truth versus meaning) is narrow. From the recipient's side, bullshit works best when its two coordinated concerns seem maximally unconnected, as when a science-education advocate turns out to be an evangelical in disguise.

chapters.file: ch26 - The Case for Purism about Bullshit.md
chapters.relation: The pragmatic definition dissolves Frankfurt's puzzle: the liar sins against the semantics of truth, while the bullshitter sins against pragmatics, disguising the effect his speech is designed to have (advancing science education) behind another (promoting evangelical Christianity). We can safely ignore bullshit, as with the coworker's Darwin rants, because without a gullible audience it has no effect, unlike the lie about whether the office milk has soured. Reisch adds that Stephen Meyer's post-Kitzmiller defiance, Willy Loman's optimism, the robber in Dog Day Afternoon, and Mamet's Glengary Glen Ross salesmen show why we even sympathize with bullshitters clinging to their creations, and that our tolerance extends to the pluralism of beliefs bullshit exploits.

chapters.file: ch27 - Chapter 4 - Bullshit and the Foibles of the Human Mind, or What the Masters of.md
chapters.relation: Reisch concludes that on the pragmatic definition there is less bullshit than 'Bullshit!'-slinging suggests: your partner announcing the relationship is over and a White House claim about an oil-rich nation eager for democracy are merely true or false announcements, not bullshit. Real bullshit is the partner engineering a blame-free breakup through talk of feeling smothered, or the claim that a dictator possesses nuclear weapons about to be used. He closes by comparing bullshit to a poem or symphony: a specific, artfully layered creation intelligently designed for pragmatic effect, which our casual use of the word obscures to the bullshitter's advantage.

chapters.file: ch28 - Some Cognitive Foibles of the Human Mind.md
chapters.relation: Kenneth Taylor opens his essay on the debased stew of bullshit, propaganda, and spin in public discourse, arguing that in an open public square the bullshitting arts must become highly refined, whereas a totalitarian state can afford crude bludgeoning, and that the marketplace of ideas has not spontaneously driven out bad discourse. His central claim: purveyors cannot sell what we do not buy, so the fault lies partly in ourselves, in built-in architectural foibles of the mind that make it permanently susceptible to manipulation. bullshit works best when we do not recognize it, and susceptibility to comforting falsehood is rooted in the mind's very architecture.

Taylor illustrates the mind's foibles with the Iraq war beliefs that held a vice-grip on believers long after disconfirming evidence, explained by confirmation bias and information cocoons like Fox News and talk radio. He walks through the classic framing experiments, the avian-flu programs that are identical when described as '2,000 saved' or '4,000 die,' showing how politicians Smith and Jones exploit framing to jointly mislead voters, and the Wason selection task, where subjects fail on abstract cards but succeed when reframed as bartender cheater-detection. Citing Stephen Pinker on evolved, domain-specific modules, he concludes that whoever controls the frame may control all, which is exactly the leverage the masters of the dark arts exploit.

Taylor draws the hopeful and bleak conclusions: our minds are fine instruments for hunter-gatherer information environments, but the modern mismatch between savannah-designed cognition and deliberately framed misinformation explains why bull, spin, and propaganda abound. The masters of the dark arts are now astute students of cognitive foibles and wield means of persuasion with unprecedented reach. His two-front response is education that instills suspicion of comforting falsehoods and the habit of re-framing, plus widening access to the means of public representation now monopolized by a self-serving elite, because 'only those who seek more than bullshit can drive it out.'

chapters.file: ch31 - Does the Bullshitter Pay Attention to the Truth.md
chapters.relation: Sara Bernal distinguishes public, interpersonal, and private bullshit (bullshitting oneself) and argues that in an era rich in public bullshit like the Iraq war, private bullshit should not be overlooked, since it is at the core of personality disorders. Departing rapidly from Frankfurt, she rejects his claim that bullshit is essentially unconnected to a concern with truth, proposing instead that core cases of bullshit have a stronger connection to truth than Frankfurt allows. Applying her revised analysis to personality disorders will, she claims, explain why their core features produce social difficulties.

Against Frankfurt's picture of the bullshitter who pays no attention to truth at all, Bernal argues the typical bullshitter is strongly connected to truth via a desire to obscure a specific part of it, conscious or not. Her prototype is the undergraduate who, knowing she has nothing thoughtful to say on an assigned essay, throws up a screen of verbiage, sometimes with malice aforethought, sometimes through a barely conscious motive to get an undeserved A. Unlike the liar she never denies the hidden truth directly but works indirectly, through pompous tone, reluctance to get to the point, and windiness, or simply by distracting the audience.

Bernal gives the Bush administration's yellowcake-from-Niger and Saddam-9/11 red herrings as distraction bullshit concealing the antecedent intention to invade Iraq, then states five features of her two-part conception: the bullshitter must attend to the one 'target' truth she wants to hide, bullshit shades into lying as awareness increases, unconscious motives do the work, non-verbal means suffice (the Newport ads), and self-bullshitting is a species of self-deception. Split-brain patients who confabulate 'that funny machine' to explain unaccountable giggling at a picture shown only to the right hemisphere ground the claim that unconscious motives are respectable neuroscience. Her account, unlike Frankfurt's, applies in psychiatry.

chapters.file: ch37 - Some Examples of Bullshit in Personality Disorders.md
chapters.relation: The essay defines personality disorder via DSM-IV as an enduring, inflexible pattern deviating from cultural expectations, and catalogs the ten disorders in three clusters: the erratic (antisocial, with the Enron crew and glib con artists as textbook cases; borderline; histrionic, from the undergrad who visits professors' office hours to talk about herself; narcissistic), the anxious (avoidant, dependent, obsessive-compulsive), and the eccentric (schizoid, schizotypal, paranoid). The clue to where bullshit lurks: wherever the afflicted is out of touch with some key aspect of reality or where her stock behavior leads others to false beliefs. The disorders' rigidity makes life 'a bad one-act play that repeats again and again.'

The essay works through the disorders case by case: the antisocial's glib charm implicates 'I am not a nasty piece of work' without saying it, the borderline's suicidal gestures implicate 'life without you is not worth living' that her contempt belies, the histrionic's shallow opinions and sexual provocativeness implant false impressions of depth, and the compensating narcissist's charade of superiority hides a dimly glimpsed core of low self-esteem. Self-directed bullshit follows: the fanatic paranoid's superhero fantasies deny that she is not extraordinary, the phobic avoidant displaces anxiety onto elevators and dogs, the self-deserting avoidant escapes into fantasy, dependents distract themselves from doubts about their caregiver, and the obsessive-compulsive buries big-picture anxiety in rules and lists.

chapters.file: ch39 - Perfect Partners Bullshit and Distorted Social Perceptions.md
chapters.relation: Surveying the catalog, the essay finds bullshit strategems that are first-rank symptoms in eight of ten disorders, quoting Frankfurt's 'each of us contributes his share' to observe that pathological personalities are notably generous contributors. Bullshitting is notably absent from the eccentric cluster: the schizoid's flat affect removes the pain-avoidance motive, and schizoids and schizotypals lack the mindreading facility successful bullshit requires. Other-bullshitting (mostly falsehood-implicating) marks the erratic cluster, self-bullshitting (mostly distraction) the anxious, and the essay closes by stressing that the disordered person is afflicted, her bullshit a personal tragedy as well as an infliction.

chapters.file: ch40 - The Threat Posed by Bullshit.md
chapters.relation: The essay's final section argues distorted social perception and bullshit are perfect partners that reinforce each other: the paranoiac imagining insults, the histrionic inhabiting a world of admirers, and the borderline seeing abandonment everywhere each see less of social reality, supplying more 'easy targets' to obscure without the sting of conscience that aware deception provokes. The compensating narcissist's glimmering of her charade and the self-deserting avoidant's glimmering of her escape show how dim awareness eases bullshitting. The street runs both ways, since hiding parts of social truth from yourself further impairs your perception, so some disorder bullshit is causally downstream of distortion while self-bullshitting deepens it.

holes.name: Rudolf Carnap
holes.what: Vienna Circle logical positivist who diagnosed metaphysical statements as meaningless pseudo-statements, most famously in his critique of Heidegger's 'Das Nichts selbst nichtet'.
holes.why: Chapter 8 presents Carnap's campaign against Heideggerian metaphysics as the twentieth century's high point of philosophy's anti-bullshit crusade.

holes.name: Logical Positivism (the Vienna Circle)
holes.what: The Vienna Circle's program holding that meaningful statements are logical truths or empirically verifiable ones and that metaphysics is sophistry and illusion.
holes.why: Chapter 8 casts the Circle's 1929 'Scientific World-Conception' as the modern apotheosis of the Enlightenment fight against bullshit that Frankfurt continues.

holes.name: Alfred Mele
holes.what: Philosopher who deflates self-deception, explaining it through motivated misinterpretation and selective evidence-gathering rather than an interpersonal deceiver-dupe model.
holes.why: Chapter 14 builds its case that bullshit can be unintentional directly on Mele's argument that self-deceivers mask evidence instead of playing deceiver and dupe at once.

holes.name: G.A. Cohen
holes.what: Political philosopher whose 'Deeper into Bullshit' replies to Frankfurt, defining bullshit by the unclarifiable unclarity of the product rather than the producer's indifference to truth.
holes.why: Chapter 14 stages the Frankfurt-Cohen debate, using Cohen's output-centered definition to explain unintentional bullshit that Frankfurt's process-centered account misses.

holes.name: Bullshit as Unclarifiable Unclarity
holes.what: Cohen's output-centered definition of bullshit: discourse marked by an obscurity that cannot be clarified, whatever the speaker's state of mind.
holes.why: Chapter 15 needs it to classify alchemy and Althusserian prose as bullshit without accusing blameless method-users like Newton of intentional indifference to truth.

holes.name: Pseudoscience (the demarcation problem)
holes.what: Claims that wear the trappings of science without its methods, raising the demarcation problem of separating genuine science from imitation science.
holes.why: Chapter 22 argues the Intelligent Design movement is bullshit precisely because it disguises religious creationism in scientific-sounding concepts like 'irreducible complexity'.

holes.name: Cognitive Bias (confirmation bias, framing effects)
holes.what: Systematic, built-in deviations from rational judgment, such as confirmation bias and framing effects, documented by cognitive and social psychology.
holes.why: Chapter 29 argues these architectural foibles of the mind explain why propaganda and bullshit take hold, from Iraq-war beliefs to information cocoons like Fox News.
